explain.say: The Quran is the holy book of Islam. Muslims believe it is the word of God, revealed in Arabic to the Prophet Muhammad through the angel Jibril, also called Gabriel, over about 23 years.

draw.text: Revealed from 610 to 632 CE, Muslims believe

explain.say: Muslims believe the first revelation came in a cave on Mount Hira near Mecca, in the month of Ramadan, beginning with the word iqra, which means read or recite. In 622 the Prophet and his followers moved to Medina, a journey called the Hijra.

draw.label: Mecca and Medina: the Hijra of 622 CE begins the Islamic calendar

draw.text: First words revealed: Surah Al-Alaq, 96:1 to 5

explain.say: The Quran has 114 chapters, called surahs, made of verses called ayat, about 6,236 in the most common count. After the short opening surah, the surahs are arranged roughly from longest to shortest.

explain.say: The surahs are known as Meccan or Medinan, depending on whether they were revealed before or after the Hijra. Meccan surahs often focus on belief in one God and the Day of Judgement, while Medinan surahs also guide community life.

a: Belief in one God, the hereafter
b: Guidance for family and community life

faq.q: How many surahs are in the Quran?
faq.a: The Quran has 114 surahs, or chapters. The longest is Al-Baqarah, with 286 verses, and the shortest is Al-Kawthar, with just 3.
asks: How many chapters are in the Quran?
What is a surah?
Which is the longest surah?

faq.q: How many verses are in the Quran?
faq.a: The most common count is 6,236 verses, called ayat. Other traditional counts differ slightly, mainly because of where verses are divided, not because the text is different.
asks: How many ayat are in the Quran?
What is an ayah?
How long is the Quran?

faq.q: Why is the Quran recited in Arabic?
faq.a: Muslims believe the Quran was revealed in Arabic and that its exact Arabic words are the word of God. Translations help people understand the meaning, but they are seen as interpretations, so prayers and recitation use the Arabic.
asks: Why do Muslims pray in Arabic?
Can the Quran be translated?
Is a translation of the Quran still the Quran?

faq.a: Al-Fatiha, the Opening, is the first surah of the Quran, with seven verses praising God and asking for guidance on the straight path. Muslims recite it in every unit of every daily prayer.
asks: What is the first surah of the Quran?
Why is Al-Fatiha important?
What does Al-Fatiha mean?

faq.a: Muslims believe the angel Jibril, also called Gabriel, brought the revelation to the Prophet Muhammad bit by bit over about 23 years, from 610 to 632 CE, beginning in a cave on Mount Hira near Mecca.
asks: Who revealed the Quran?
How long did it take to reveal the Quran?
Where was the Quran revealed?

faq.q: What were the first words revealed in the Quran?
faq.a: Muslims believe the first words revealed were the opening verses of Surah Al-Alaq, the 96th surah, beginning with iqra, read or recite, in the name of your Lord who created.
asks: What was the first revelation?
What does iqra mean?
Which verses came first?

faq.a: Muslims believe the Quran is the word of God, not written by any person; the Prophet Muhammad received it and recited it, and his companions memorised it and wrote it down. It was gathered into one book soon after his death.
asks: Who is the author of the Quran?
Did Muhammad write the Quran?
Who compiled the Quran?

faq.a: After the short opening surah, Al-Fatiha, the surahs are arranged roughly from longest to shortest, not in the order they were revealed. Many Muslims believe the Prophet himself set this order, guided by revelation.
asks: Is the Quran in chronological order?
Why are the surahs in that order?
How are the chapters of the Quran ordered?

faq.q: What are Meccan and Medinan surahs?
faq.a: Meccan surahs were revealed before the move to Medina in 622 CE and Medinan surahs after it. In the usual classification there are about 86 Meccan and 28 Medinan surahs.
asks: What is the difference between Meccan and Medinan surahs?
How many Medinan surahs are there?
What is a Meccan surah?

faq.a: A hafiz is a person who has memorised the entire Quran by heart. Millions of Muslims around the world, many of them children, have done this, continuing a tradition that goes back to the Prophet's companions.
asks: Can people memorise the whole Quran?
What does hafiz mean?
How do people learn the Quran by heart?

faq.a: A juz is one of 30 roughly equal parts of the Quran. Dividing it this way makes it easy to read the whole Quran in a month, and many Muslims do so during Ramadan.
asks: Why is the Quran divided into 30 parts?
How do Muslims read the Quran in Ramadan?
What is a para of the Quran?

faq.q: How did the Quran become one book?
faq.a: During the Prophet's life the verses were memorised and written on materials such as parchment and bone. Soon after his death they were gathered under the first caliph, Abu Bakr, and around 650 CE the caliph Uthman sent standard copies to the main cities.
asks: Who compiled the Quran into a book?
When was the Quran written down?
What is the Uthmanic codex?

faq.a: Tajwid is the set of rules for reciting the Quran correctly and beautifully: how each letter is pronounced, where to pause and which sounds to lengthen. Skilled reciters are admired across the Muslim world.
asks: How is the Quran recited?
What are the rules of Quran recitation?
Why does Quran recitation sound like singing?

faq.q: How do Muslims treat the Quran?
faq.a: Many Muslims handle the Arabic Quran with great respect: they make wudu, ritual washing, before touching it, keep it in a clean high place and never put things on top of it. They also read it, study it and seek guidance from it daily.
asks: Why do Muslims wash before touching the Quran?
How should the Quran be handled?
Why is the Quran kept high?

facts: The Quran has 114 surahs; the most common count gives 6,236 verses.
Muslims believe the Quran was revealed to the Prophet Muhammad over about 23 years, from 610 to 632 CE.
Al-Fatiha, the first surah, has seven verses and is recited in every unit of the daily prayers.
The longest surah is Al-Baqarah, with 286 verses, and the shortest is Al-Kawthar, with 3.
The Quran is divided into 30 parts, each called a juz, which many Muslims read through during Ramadan.
Fragments of a Quran manuscript at the University of Birmingham were radiocarbon dated in 2015 to between 568 and 645 CE.
